title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup

epigraph.quote: Never buy a stock that is more than 10% to 15% above its 10-week moving average or 30-week Stage 2 base—not because the trend is broken, but because the rubber band snaps back toward institutional support.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein / William O'Neil Trend Discipline

web_blocks.html: Laurus Labs remains a premier momentum leader in Indian healthcare, sitting firmly inside a confirmed Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend with a 97.1 relative strength percentile (thewrap_stage2) and +150.51% 1-year return [23]. Across our two verified sessions, the stock closed at ₹2,370.70 on the 2026-11-23 NSE market-facts ledger (+3.32% 1D, +29.90% 3M, 63D RS +25.29%) and advanced to ₹2,460.00 on the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot (+3.77% 1D, +25.51% 1M)—just -1.13% below its 52-week high of ₹2,488.00 [23].

Despite a tightening 11.75% Bollinger Band width just below ₹2,488.00, the multi-timeframe tape still flashes an unmistakable extension warning (CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT). On the 2026-11-25 weekly chart (1W), RSI(14) sits in overbought territory at 74.09, with price stretched +36.32% above the rising 30-week SMA (₹1,804.52) and +10.55% above the 10-week EMA (₹2,225.28) [23]. On the daily chart (1D), price trades +14.68% above the 50-day SMA (₹2,145.14) and +57.45% above the 200-day SMA (₹1,562.42), with Daily RSI(14) at 63.83. On the 4-hour chart (4H), RSI(14) is 64.43 above the 4H 20-EMA (₹2,349.97) and 4H 50-SMA (₹2,269.48).

web_blocks.text: Institutional Sponsorship, Insider Supply Absorption & Upward Stop-Loss Ratchet
web_blocks.title: Institutional Sponsorship, Insider Supply Absorption & Upward Stop-Loss Ratchet

web_blocks.html: Volume and ownership tape reveal a subtle tug-of-war beneath the surface. On the positive side, FII ownership expanded steadily to 30.84% in September 2026 (up from 25.82% in March 2026), and the 2026-11-25 +3.77% advance cleared 2.98M shares (1.18x the 30-day average of 2.52M) [1][23]. That shows institutional buyers have so far absorbed the 20.7 lakh shares sold by CEO Dr. Chava and CFO Ravi Kumar on November 11–12 [28][29]. On the cautionary side, the 2026-11-23 NSE ledger logged 7 distribution days over the prior 25 sessions on Laurus against a broader Indian market classified as Uptrend (narrow breadth)—with only 55.2% of the 500-stock breadth pool above the 50-DMA, 48.2% above the 200-DMA, and 3 Nifty distribution days.

For existing shareholders, this exact tape calls for an upward-only stop-loss ratchet rather than panic selling. Because the 30-week SMA has climbed from ₹1,719.85 (Nov 13) to ₹1,804.52 (Nov 25) and the 50-day SMA has risen from ₹2,084.47 to ₹2,145.14, we ratchet our structural invalidation stop upward by +4.73% from ₹1,684.88 to ₹1,764.51 (anchored between the 30W SMA at ₹1,804.52 and the 40W EMA at ₹1,731.40) [23]. We also raise our tactical trailing trim guardrail from ₹2,085.00 to ₹2,145.00 (50-DMA / just above Pivot S1 ₹2,090.83). With a 14-day ATR of ₹80.02 (3.25% daily range), the ₹1,764.51 structural stop sits -28.3% below live CMP (8.7x ATR)—reinforcing why new cash should never chase at ₹2,460.00 without a base reset [23].

book_paragraphs: If Chapter 7 showed us that Laurus Labs is expensive on fundamentals and prolonged capex, Chapter 8 explains why the share price has kept climbing: relentless institutional momentum. On the weekly chart, Laurus Labs remains firmly inside a Stan Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend, sporting a 97.1 relative strength percentile and a 150.5% one-year return.

Tracking our two verified market dates shows how fast this tape moves. On the 23 November 2026 NSE market-facts ledger, Laurus closed at ₹2,370.70—4.7% off its 52-week high. Two sessions later, on our 25 November 2026 live TradingView snapshot, the stock surged 3.77% on 2.98 million shares (1.18x its 30-day average) to ₹2,460.00, sitting just 1.13% shy of its ₹2,488.00 52-week high.

That strong volume absorption is telling. It confirms that institutional demand—led by foreign institutional investors whose stake climbed from 25.82% in March 2026 to 30.84% by September 2026—has so far absorbed the 20.7 lakh shares sold by CEO Dr. Chava and CFO Ravi Kumar on November 11–12. For existing shareholders, there is no technical trend break that would justify panic-dumping a winning Stage 2 leader.

At the same time, every momentum gauge warns that new cash chasing at ₹2,460.00 is stepping onto a stretched rubber band. On the 25 November live chart, Laurus sits 10.55% above its 10-week EMA (₹2,225.28), 14.68% above its 50-day SMA (₹2,145.14), 36.32% above its 30-week SMA (₹1,804.52), and 57.45% above its 200-day SMA (₹1,562.42). Weekly RSI(14) remains overbought at 74.09, while Daily RSI is 63.83 and 4-Hour RSI is 64.43.

Context from the broader Indian equity tape amplifies that caution. As of the 23 November 2026 ledger, the Nifty 50 sits in an Uptrend with narrow breadth: only 55.2% of the 500-stock pool trades above its 50-day moving average and just 48.2% above its 200-day moving average, alongside 3 Nifty distribution days. Inside that narrow tape, Laurus itself logged 7 distribution days over the past 25 sessions on the ledger. Narrow-breadth uptrends routinely punish late breakouts with sudden 10% to 15% air-pockets back to the 50-day moving average.

Because Laurus Labs has no liquid NSE F&O options chain—confirmed as NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID in our 25 November options snapshot—you cannot rent upside cheaply through a defined-risk call spread or LEAPS contract. Every rupee of risk must be managed directly in cash equity, where the 14-day Average True Range is ₹80.02 (3.25% of CMP) and the structural invalidation stop sits 28.3% below today's live price.

This technical map gives us a crisp, mechanical discipline for both seats. For existing holders, we apply our upward-only stop-loss ratchet: as the rising 30-week SMA moved up to ₹1,804.52 and the 50-day SMA climbed to ₹2,145.14, we raise our structural invalidation stop from ₹1,684.88 to ₹1,764.51 (+4.73%) and lift our trailing trim guardrail from ₹2,085.00 to ₹2,145.00. For new capital, we refuse to chase a 74.09 weekly RSI at ₹2,460.00 when the nearest institutional support band sits below at ₹2,191.90–₹2,344.77.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Respect the Trend, Ratchet the Floor
paragraphs: Two truths coexist on this chart: Laurus Labs is an intact Stage 2 institutional leader that absorbed 20.7 lakh insider shares, yet it is tactically extended in a narrow-breadth market. Ratcheting stops upward protects existing profits while refusing to chase preserves new cash.
